To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin alone or in combination with glucagon, when infused into the portal circulation of dogs after portocaval shunt, can prevent atrophy of the liver and can stimulate cell renewal.
insulin alone, but not glucagon alone or glucagon/insulin mixtures, preserves liver morphology and cell division after complete portacaval shunting in dogs.
Insulin, glucagons, and their combination have been infused for 4 days into the left and right hepatic portal vein of dogs that had previously been subjected to portacaval anastomosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
liver regeneration after portacaval anastomosis.
the pathogenesis and treatment of liver atrophy, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
the study of the pathophysiology, treatment and prevention of hepatic encephalopathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin, but not glucagon, can reverse the atrophy of hepatocytes after portacaval anastomoses.
the liver is a dynamic, hormonally controlled organ that can be maintained in a healthy state by insulin, but that the insulin benefit can be reduced or negated by large doses of glucagon.
insulin alone can reverse the atrophy of the left liver lobe after complete portacaval shunting, and this effect can be enhanced by the addition of glucagon to the insulin infusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin is a growth-promoting hormone, glucagon is not, and the two hormones may act antagonistically.
insulin and glucagon have opposing effects on hepatocyte growth and that glucagon may inhibit insulin action.

insulin and glucagon are important regulators of liver cell renewal, that the liver is a target for insulin and glucagon, that the liver has receptors for insulin and glucagen and that the liver is an important target organ for insulin and glucogen in the control of cell growth and cell renewal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin is the most important hormone in liver growth and regeneration.
insulin is an effective treatment for the liver atrophy that occurs after portacaval anastomosis.
insulin and glucagon are the two hormones that are most intimately involved in the control of hepatocyte proliferation in vivo, and that insulin is the dominant one of the two.
